text: My wife and I built Lullwatch because of our
own first pregnancy.
When the contraction started,
we had one question and nothing we had could answer it.
Is this it?
Do we go now or do we wait?
We learned that this is one of the hardest
calls in late pregnancy.
Go in too early and you're sent home.
In a study of over 1,600 first-time mothers,
one in three went to hospital before their
contractions were five minutes apart.
Those early arrivals were more likely to end
in a caesarean, about one in four,
against about one in six,
but leave it too late and the journey itself
becomes the risk.
So we looked for an app to help,
but the apps that could help want the most
private data there is.
When Mozilla reviewed 25 pregnancy and period apps,
18 got its privacy warning.
And in 2025,
a US jury found Meta liable for collecting
data from the Flo app, including pregnancy data.
So we built Lullwatch, a private labour
companion that tells her when to pack and when
to leave for the hospital.
Its AI runs on sealed hardware on NEAR AI Cloud,
and her own phone checks the proof.
Setup is three questions.
Is this her first baby, which hospital,
and how long the journey takes?
Lullwatch applies the standard rule for her,
if her midwife gave her different numbers,
those win.
When a contraction starts, she taps.
When it ends, she taps again.
Or, hands-free, she just says now, and stop.
The log never leaves her phone.
A few hours in, the gaps are shrinking.
Fixed, tested rules watch the trend,
forecast when she'll meet her midwife's rule,
subtract the journey, and give her a time,
start packing,
leave by this time.
When it's time to call the maternity unit,
she doesn't have to think.
She taps Call midwife,
and the sealed AI writes exactly what to say
from her timer.
Every number is checked against the timer
before she sees it.
And if something feels wrong,
like bleeding,
or the baby moving less,
the count doesn't matter anymore.
Lullwatch says go now.
Rules decide.
The AI only explains.
She can ask it anything.
Her question is encrypted on her phone to a
key only the sealed hardware holds.
Then her phone checks for itself,
NVIDIA confirms the GPUs,
Intel confirms the enclave is up to date,
and every reply is signed inside it.
Nobody can read her labour,
not even us.
That's what NEAR AI Cloud makes possible.
Private AI you can verify,
not just trust.
We built the app we wished we'd had.
Lullwatch is free, open source,
and works offline.
Know when to go.
